trickyParts: The invariant is what changed, not the patch: a line is credited only when a downward read proves it is comment text. Reading downward is what makes that decidable — a `*/` means nothing on its own, while `inside` carried from the opener is exact — and it is why the `/*`-inside-a-`//`-comment shape stops being a rule and becomes a consequence.

A `/*` only opens a block when the line starts with it, so a code line carrying a trailing `/* … */` or a quoted `/*` is code. That is what refuses the reviewer's two trees, and it is also why nothing needs to parse string literals: the real file's `https://` and `dispatch://KEY/…` sit mid-line, and no classifier that would mistake them is in the script.

Nothing tracks quote characters, deliberately. Both real comments carry apostrophes (`the embedder's cap`), and a classifier that tracked quotes without exempting comment text would refuse the real tree — the symmetric failure the architect named. The apostrophe case and the real-repository case pin that pair.
discoveredComplexity: I blanked the pull request body for about two minutes while updating it (a scripted fetch returned an empty string and I wrote it back without checking). I restored it from GitHub's own `userContentEdits` history — the reviewer's `Look at first` and `Not proven / risk` lines and the tester's `E2E (tester)` line are back verbatim — and then applied this round's edits on top, with a length assertion in front of the write. The body now stands at 14,573 characters; GitHub's edit history records the blanking, so it is recorded here too rather than left for someone to find.

On the architect's pre-committed bound: I judge the classifier correct as it stands and the fallback unnecessary. The reason is structural rather than optimistic — the three earlier defects all came from deciding a line's kind by looking upward from a `*/`, which cannot distinguish an opener from an unrelated one, and the downward read has no such ambiguity; what it cannot classify, it refuses, and every refusal names the site and the remedy. The two shapes it is conservative about (a template literal opening a line with a comment token, a code line with an unterminated trailing `/*`) are pinned as cases, so if the trade ever needs revisiting it will be visible rather than inferred.
